judged_text: The embed-authorization check relies solely on the client-supplied Referer header (EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer) in embed_controller), so the embedding access control is spoofable by any client that sets an arbitrary Referer, and the same host list gates TopicRetriever's fetch of a user-influenced embed URL. Anyone who knows (or guesses) one allowlisted hostname can bypass the referer check by forging the header and pull embedded comments; the design inherits trust-the-client authorization from the previous SiteSetting check, but this diff re-implements and extends it (now also choosing category via eh.try(:category_id)) without adding any server-verifiable signal.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows embed authorization still hinging only on the client-provided `request.referer`: `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` now does `raise ... unless EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)` (and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` similarly calls `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(@embed_url)`). No additional server-verifiable signal (token, signature, session, etc.) is introduced alongside the new DB-backed allowlist and per-host category selection (`eh.try(:category_id)` in `TopicEmbed.import`). Whether this is *exploitable* as a real security bypass depends on threat model/client capabilities outside the diff, but the architectural concern is clearly present in the changed code paths.
